newsitem.title: CHINA: China central bank expands open market operations.
newsitem.headline: China central bank expands open market operations.

text.p: China's central bank will increasingly rely on open market operations and move away from administrative measures to control money supply, state media on Friday quoted deputy governor Chen Yaoxian as saying.
The People's Bank of China wanted to rely more on interest rates and move away from fixed lending quotas, the official China Securities quoted him as telling a banking conference.
However, quotas still had a role in what he described as a transitional stage of the financial system.
As part of efforts to rely more on on market mechanisms, the central bank wanted to sharply expand interbank trading to create a unified, national market.
Chen gave no timetable for the plan but said this would require a major expansion of the use of treasury debt, central bank paper and state policy debt as money market tools.
The bank official said the central bank planned to merge its two types of bank reserves into a single reserve that would be used more effectively to control money supply.
The central bank wanted to see a reasonable adjustment between the deposit and lending rates, Chen said.
Banks in the past had complained that lending rates were too low compared to deposit levels.

In the past, state banks were particularly unhappy with an interest rate subsidy -- meant to attract long-term bank deposits in a period of high inflation. That brought in deposits but banks were unable to lend the funds profitably.
The interest rate subsidy was scrapped on new deposits last year but banks have continued to complain about the interest rate structure.
